questions.q: Solve $3^{x+1} = 81$ exactly.
Solve $5^{2x} = 17$. Give an exact answer and a decimal to three places.
Solve $e^{2x} - 5e^x + 6 = 0$ exactly.
Solve $\ln(2x - 3) = 1$. Give an exact answer and a decimal to three places.
Solve $\log_2 x + \log_2(x - 6) = 4$, checking for extraneous solutions.
questions.answer: $\log_2\left(x(x - 6)\right) = 4$, so $x^2 - 6x - 16 = 0$, giving $(x - 8)(x + 2) = 0$. Reject $x = -2$ (logarithm of a negative number): $x = 8$.

The pH of a solution is $\mathrm{pH} = -\log[\mathrm{H^+}]$. Find the hydrogen-ion concentration $[\mathrm{H^+}]$ of a solution with pH 4.6, in scientific notation to two significant figures.
Solve $2^{x} = 3^{x-1}$, giving an exact expression and a decimal to three places.
Solve $4^x - 3\cdot2^x - 4 = 0$ exactly, using the substitution $u = 2^x$.
A bacteria culture grows according to $N(t) = 500e^{kt}$. If the population reaches 2000 after 6 hours, find $k$ (4 d.p.) and hence the time for the population to reach 10,000, to one decimal place.
Solve the equation $e^{x} + e^{-x} = 3$ exactly, using the substitution $u = e^x$ (this expression is related to $2\cosh x$).
questions.answer: Multiply by $u=e^x$: $u^2 - 3u + 1 = 0$, so $u = \frac{3\pm\sqrt{5}}{2}$. Both roots are positive, giving $x = \ln\left(\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2}\right)$ or $x = \ln\left(\frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}\right)$.

sections.heading: Equations requiring both exponential and logarithmic techniques

questions.q: Solve $\log_2(x)=3-\log_2(x-2)$, checking for extraneous solutions.
Solve $e^{\ln x+\ln2}=10$ for $x$, simplifying the exponent first.
For the equation $5^{2x}=17$ solved earlier ($x\approx0.880$), verify the solution by substituting back and computing both sides to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer: $5^{2(0.880)}=5^{1.76}\approx17.02$, matching the right side $17$ (small rounding difference due to the decimal approximation of $x$), confirming the solution.

questions.q: A population model is $P(t)=800e^{0.05t}$. Find the time $t$ when $P(t)=2000$, to two decimal places, and separately find $P^{-1}(1500)$ (the time when the population reaches 1500), to two decimal places.
Verify the solution $x=8$ found earlier for $\log_2x+\log_2(x-6)=4$ by substituting back into the original equation.
Solve $\ln(x)+\ln(x-3)=\ln(10)$, checking for extraneous solutions.

A radioactive sample decays according to $A(t)=A_0e^{-0.08t}$. If the initial amount is 500 g, find the time $t$ (to two decimal places) at which only 50 g remains, and separately find the time at which 90% of the original sample has decayed away.
questions.answer: For $A=50$: $50=500e^{-0.08t} \Rightarrow 0.1=e^{-0.08t} \Rightarrow t=\frac{\ln0.1}{-0.08}\approx28.79$. For 90% decayed, 10% remains ($A=50$ g as well, since $10\%$ of $500$ is $50$): this is the same equation, so $t\approx28.79$ — confirming both descriptions refer to the same instant.
